scenes.title: The Morning You Decided to Stay

default: You wake in Crestfall on the seventeenth day, and you know, quite clearly, that you are not leaving.
You decided last night. This morning it is simply so, as things are once the deciding is over. It is no longer a question, and no longer a weight. It is only the way things are.

[missing person] is up before you. They are at the window, looking down at the market square. In the morning light the square is doing something it has not done for weeks. It is busy. It isn't crowded, but it is busy, which is not the same thing. People are going about as though there were things worth doing today.

default.text: On your last day in the ruins you went to the gate stones once more. You had found the name in the old man's entries. "Joren," you said.
He looked up from the figure in his hands. "Yes," he said.

text.commander:
You stand beside them at the window and look at the market as you would look at a position that has been taken and now wants running rather than defending.

"We need to make a list," you say.

They look at you. Then, slowly, they smile. It is the first real smile since you found them in the ruins, not the careful one, but the one you remember from before.

"Always," they say. "Always with the lists."
text.arcane:
Crestfall feels different this morning from yesterday. It is only a little different, but it is different in the right direction.

You make a note in your journal: day seventeen, first readings taken.

You have decided to stay, and you have decided to write down everything. Ashenveld is the most important place you will ever have the chance to study, and you have just committed yourself to spending years in it. You are quite aware that this is either the best decision you have ever made or the worst, and that it may be years before you know which.
text.ranger:
The birds are back in the market square this morning. There are two sparrows, and something bigger that you can't put a name to at once, a bird that usually keeps further into the ordinary forest and is coming nearer now that the forest is becoming ordinary again.

You will see it again tomorrow, and the day after, and the day after that. How the creatures of Ashenveld come back will be the plainest measure of what the seal has done.

[missing person] is at the window. You stand beside them and watch the birds.
text.cipher:
You walk round the market this morning as somebody who lives here now, and it looks different.

Different things matter, and different people need handling in different ways. What hold you have got on people these last weeks will have to be turned into something that lasts.

You are going to be here a while, and you had better start thinking like it.

choices.text: Decide what comes first. What does Ashenveld need most just now?

success.text:
You think it through, and the answer is plain. You need to know how things stand: what the seal has done and what it hasn't, what the afflicted need now, and how quickly the land will mend. None of the rest of it, the rebuilding or the managing of people or the account, can be done well without knowing that.

So you and [missing person] spend the first day of your new life in Ashenveld finding out, carefully, and writing it all down for anyone to read.

success_at_cost.text:
You work out what needs doing, but there is more of it than there is day. You have to choose what comes first, and some of your choices are wrong in ways you won't discover until later.

That is what it is to stay somewhere. It is never quite finished.

failure.text:
Everything wants doing at once. You spend your first day of staying in Ashenveld dealing with one urgent thing after another, and never get them into any order.

In the evening [missing person] sits down across from you and says, "Tomorrow. We start again tomorrow." The patience in their voice is one of the things you came here for.

default: You and [missing person] leave Crestfall on the seventeenth day.

You take the west road. It is not the way you came in. It goes out of Ashenveld into the rest of the world, where there are no ruins under the forests, and no curse in the wells, and nobody going quietly dim.
It is an ordinary morning, overcast, and cold as late autumn is cold in this part of the world.
You walk, and they walk beside you. Crestfall falls behind you at the pace of walking, which is slow enough to see everything you pass, and fast enough that going back would mean deciding to.

default.text: On your last day in the ruins you went to the gate stones once more. You had found the name in the old man's entries. "Joren," you said.
He looked up from the figure in his hands. "Yes," he said.

text.commander:
You take with you what you came with: your pack, your training, and what you know about the ruins and what was done about them.

You left Crestfall without telling Vorne everything. He was promised an account, and [missing person] will send it in the end, from wherever you finish up. It will be complete. You gave your word.

The west road runs on between ordinary trees, and you walk.
text.arcane:
You carry your journal, and the copy you made of [missing person]'s fourteen months of notes in the days before you left.

You are leaving the most important place you will ever have to study, because the person beside you matters more. You leave it behind you, and go.

You walk the west road, and write as you walk, because that is the sort of person you are.
text.ranger:
On the west road the forest is ordinary. There are birds, and there are deer of the right kind, moving as they should, who notice you and work out properly whether you are dangerous.

You are not. You are two people walking away from one thing and towards another that hasn't got a name yet.

The forest is ordinary, and after weeks in Ashenveld, ordinary is very nearly too much.
text.cipher:
You are thinking beyond Ashenveld already. The world is large, you have your skills, and beside you is somebody who spent fourteen months learning things that nobody else knows.

The two of you would be worth a great deal to the wrong people. You are already thinking how to keep it out of their hands.

choices.text: Talk about where you're going, and what comes after Ashenveld.

default.text:
You walk a mile before either of you says anything.

Then [missing person] says, "I want to go somewhere I have never been."

"That's most places," you say.

"Yes," they say. "That is the point."

You walk on. Three miles out of Crestfall the west road meets the high road at a crossroads. Left goes north and right goes south, and straight on goes west to the coast.

"Which one?" they say.

You look at all three, and choose one, and don't say why.

choices.text: Walk without talking. Some leavings have to be felt before they can be talked about.

default.text:
You don't talk. You walk.

It is the silence of two people who have been through something together and have not yet found words for what it means that it is over.

At the crossroads you stop, and so do they.

You look at each other.

"Right or left?" they say.

You choose, and you go.

default: They have gone. You watched them leave the Tallow and cross the market square, and you are still sitting at your table.
Aldous brings you something without being asked. He has been an innkeeper long enough to know when a person wants something in their hand and would rather not have to ask for it.
He nods. He doesn't remind you that you said much the same about Ashenveld when you first came. He is too good at his work for that.

default.text: On your last day in the ruins you went to the gate stones once more. You had found the name in the old man's entries. "Joren," you said.
He looked up from the figure in his hands. "Yes," he said.

text.commander:
A week, perhaps two. There are things you promised to see through: the account, the arrangement with the Compact, and the formal recognition of the Rootless camp. None of them will hold unless they are properly tied off.

You made a promise, and you don't leave promises hanging.
text.arcane:
The account has to be finished before you go: [missing person]'s notes, and what you saw yourself, and Pol's learning, the whole story of what happened in the ruins and what it means.

It is a week's work, perhaps longer. You will do it in the time you have.
text.ranger:
Somebody needs to write down how the land is mending now, before you leave: how it is now, which way it is going, and how fast. And somebody needs to know what to look for, and how to read it.

You spend the first morning teaching Branch. He is a better pupil than he lets on.
text.cipher:
The arrangements are fragile until suddenly they aren't. You have a week, perhaps two, to make them less so.

You know this kind of work. You have left places before. You know what has to be done before you go, so that what you built is less likely to fall down without you.

choices.text: Decide what must be done before you can leave.

success.text:
You make the list. There is the account to finish. There is the arrangement with the Compact to be put in writing. There is the camp's recognition, to be made formal before Vorne can find an excuse to put it off. And there is a talk to be had with Pol about what she will do next.

It is seven days' work, and you have seven days. It will only just fit.

success_at_cost.text:
There is more on the list than seven days will hold. You have to decide what comes first, and what to leave to Maret and Branch to manage without you.

You don't always decide rightly. Some of what you leave behind will go wrong, and you will never hear of it. That is the price of leaving.

failure.text:
There is more on the list than there is time, and you can't make the list any shorter. You will do what you can and leave the rest.

Some time in the second week you will look up from your work and see that you are not going to finish, and you will have to decide whether to stay longer or go with it undone. That is still to come.

default: The door of the Tallow shuts behind them, and you are alone at your table.
Aldous says nothing. He has kept a bar long enough to know when it is best to say nothing at all.

You sit with what you chose. You don't regret it. You don't know yet whether it is the sort of choice anybody could regret. It is the sort that has consequences, and you will find out what they are by living through them.
Outside, Crestfall is beginning its seventeenth day. It is going slowly, like a place that has lost a great deal and is finding out, a little at a time, that it has not lost everything.

default.text: On your last day in the ruins you went to the gate stones once more. You had found the name in the old man's entries. "Joren," you said.
He looked up from the figure in his hands. "Yes," he said.

text.commander:
You made a choice, and you are the sort of person who makes a choice and keeps to it.

The one you let go will understand, or they won't. Either way, you are here, and so is Ashenveld, and so is the work.

You go and find Maret. You have things to talk about.
text.arcane:
It is a little while before you feel how lonely it is. It doesn't come at the time. It comes twenty minutes later, when you look up from the table and see the empty seat across from you, which will be empty for a long while.

You write that down too, with everything else.

Then you get on with your notes.
text.ranger:
You chose to stay, and they chose to go.

You go outside, into the market square. The birds are about this morning, and Crestfall is beginning to mend. It isn't healed, and it isn't well, but it is alive, and going the right way.

You are part of the reason it is going the right way, and that is why you are staying. The other reason, walking away along the west road, you keep somewhere else.
text.cipher:
You let them go, and you are staying.

The work in Ashenveld doesn't stop because your own affairs have become complicated. It still has to be done. You have done harder work when you felt a good deal worse.

You go and find Vorne. The account has to be finished, and the camp needs its formal recognition. There is a hard week's work ahead, and you mean to do it.

choices.text: Hold to your choice. Ashenveld is where you are. Begin the work.

success.text:
You hold to it.

There is nothing solemn about it. You have made hard choices before. You keep them by doing them, day after day, not by deciding once.

You get up, and go to the Rootless camp, and begin.

success_at_cost.text:
You hold to it, but it costs you more than you had reckoned. The first day is the worst, because you have chosen and don't yet know whether you chose rightly.

You do the work anyway. The work is what you have.

failure.text:
It doesn't come easily. You sit at the table far longer than you meant to, held there by something you can't put a name to.

At last Aldous says, "The camp sent someone looking for you this morning," and puts a note on the table.

It is from Branch, and it has three words on it: we need you.

That is enough, and you go.

default: You don't remember how it ended.

default.text:
You wake under canvas, with the smell of the camp fire and somebody's coat over you. It is morning, and you have lost a day.

Maret is sitting on an upturned crate by the tent flap. "Branch carried you," she says. "Do not thank him. He will not know what to do with it."

You wake on a pallet at the back of the shrine, under the grey banner. It is morning, and a day has gone.

Edric is lighting the candles one at a time. "You were found on the steps," he says, without turning round.

You wake by the fire in the outskirts. The light is the same grey as always, but [missing person] tells you a day has gone.

"You stopped," they say. "In the middle of a sentence. I talked to you until you came back."

You wake in a room at the Tallow with your boots still on. The light says it is morning, and the wrong morning, too, for a day has gone. Somebody has left water by the bed and a heel of bread on a plate.

Aldous is in the doorway. "Two of them brought you in," he says. "I didn't ask where from."

default: You sit up. Your hands are steady enough.

default.text: You get dressed and go back out.
